source.title: Feature Learning Beyond the Edge of Stability

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains MLPs with SGD and measures loss and an effective stability ratio at large learning rates. This bears conceptually on V5, but uses a different model, loss, and sharpness measure from the claim version.
record.gate_note: The MNIST experiments report training loss, effective sharpness, stability ratio, and soft rank. The paper cites prior work on the edge of stability; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses edge-of-stability research to develop and evaluate preconditioned SGD. Its experiments measure MNIST cross-entropy loss and a minibatch, update-direction-dependent effective sharpness. They do not establish recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit under squared loss, or sharpness hovering at the Hessian stability threshold under full-batch training, as V5 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: their gradient scaling combined with quadratic width tapering permits training beyond the effective EOS, improves feature soft rank, and implicitly regularizes effective sharpness in their MNIST MLP experiments. The abstract says beyond the EOS; the experimental discussion specifically says far beyond the effective EOS. These results do not establish the corresponding claim for maximum Hessian eigenvalue sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a homogeneous νP MLP, SGD, MNIST classification loss, and an effective sharpness measure. Its experiments include a proposed layerwise gradient scaling scheme; they do not implement the squared-loss or full-batch-GD setups described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with width exponent, gradient scaling, and learning rate; the paper reports numerical errors for unscaled r = 0, occasional recoverable catapult events for unscaled r = 1 and r = 2, and successful loss descent in all tested scaled r = 2 cases.

fits_no_version.finding: Unscaled SGD produces numerical errors for some constant-width runs; linearly and quadratically tapered networks avoid these errors more successfully but exhibit occasional recoverable loss spikes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In eight-hidden-layer νP ReLU MLPs trained on MNIST with minibatch cross-entropy, tapered widths improve numerical stability, while recoverable catapult events can still occur.

fits_no_version.finding: With quadratic width tapering and proposed gradient scaling, loss descends at every tested learning rate from 2 to 16 while training remains beyond the effective EOS; larger rates yield lower effective sharpness and higher feature soft rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depthwise preconditioned SGD can reduce MNIST cross-entropy beyond its update-direction-dependent effective EOS in the tested νP MLPs.

record.problems: Empirical demonstration is limited to νP MLPs on MNIST. Results are presented in plots with qualitative descriptions and no uncertainty estimates. The text does not identify which unscaled r = 0 learning rates produce numerical errors, and does not specify which learning rates have non-descending loss when η is too large.
record.rows_left_out: No additional text-described outcomes meeting the row criteria were omitted. Figure-only exact values were not transcribed.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh training, and normalization-free residual training.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, training speed, and trainable depth; the study uses one initialization recipe.

Squared-loss recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit, curvature reduction during that recovery, divergence boundaries, and full-batch Hessian sharpness dynamics, including divergence from below the threshold.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Recoverable catapults are actual observed behavior, but occur outside V5's specified setups. Neither those recoveries nor numerical failures warrant limits_scope: V5 already allows both recovery and divergence. The supplied figure text contains axes and legends without readable trajectories, so exact rates, thresholds, and endpoint losses cannot be inferred.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size and early stopping.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems and spurious local minima across widths.
Plain versus residual networks and depth-related training error.
Comparisons of initialization schemes and their effect on trainability.

The experiments do not use squared loss or full-batch GD, and do not test the catapult mechanism or the Hessian sharpness threshold. They instead use MNIST classification, SGD, and effective sharpness under layerwise gradient scaling.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: νP ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Unscaled SGD across learning rates η = 0.2 to 1.6.
rows.measure: Minibatch loss during training; numerical errors at large learning rates.
rows.value: For r = 0, a color disappearing before t = 2000 indicates numerical errors.
rows.note: The paper describes the plot's disappearing color as numerical errors; the text does not identify which learning rates produced them.
rows.check: Numerical errors are reported, but the affected learning rates and their relation to the initial stability threshold are unspecified. This SGD cross-entropy experiment cannot establish V5's divergence regime.

rows.subject: νP ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Unscaled SGD across learning rates η = 0.2 to 1.6.
rows.baseline: Unscaled SGD with r = 0, described as having numerical errors at some settings.
rows.value: Width exponent r = 1 helps avoid numerical errors and leads to somewhat lower effective sharpness, but occasional catapult events disrupt training and the process recovers afterwards.
rows.note: The text groups r = 1 and r = 2 when describing these outcomes; this row records the r = 1 setting separately.
rows.check: Recoverable catapult events are explicitly reported for unscaled SGD, but neither squared loss nor the initial linearized-model stability threshold is tested. Effective sharpness is not the maximum Hessian eigenvalue. The result is related to V5 without measuring its specified effect.

rows.subject: νP ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: SGD with proposed gradient scaling (1), across learning rates η = 2.0 to 16.0.
rows.measure: Minibatch loss, effective sharpness, stability ratio, and last hidden layer soft rank.
rows.value: The loss successfully descends in all cases; increasing learning rates consistently lead to smaller effective sharpness and higher last hidden layer soft rank, while training takes place far beyond the effective EOS.
rows.note: The paper describes the qualitative outcomes across the plotted learning-rate settings; exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: This combines several measures of the proposed method's performance. Successful loss descent beyond its preconditioned effective EOS does not establish recovery above V5's initial linearized-model threshold or full-batch Hessian-threshold dynamics. Soft rank measures representation geometry and bears on no listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
